newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Camelot poised to run TV game show - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Camelot poised to run TV game show - paper.

text.p: Camelot, the UK operator of the national lottery, is set to receive permission within the next two weeks to run a television game show for scratch card winners with prizes of up to 100,000 pounds, the Financial Times reported.

The newspaper said in its Monday edition that the company hoped the TV game shown by the BBC would boost Instants, the lottery scratch cards which have seen sales slump to 15 million per week from 40 million per week when they were launched two years ago.

Camelot also confirmed it would prepare loyalty bonus packages for all its 650 staff later this year. The deals are designed to keep them in place until its seven-year contract to run the lottering ends in 2001, the FT said.
On Friday, Camelot executives agreed to pay part of their future bonuses to charity after the size of the payments fueled a bitter row with the government.

The new Labour government expressed outrage two weeks ago when it emerged that bonus payments had inflated Camelot's wage bill by 40 percent to 2.3 million pounds while the sum the lottery raised for charities fell.
